notes.meaning: Jonathan gives the warning signal that will mean danger. If he tells the boy that the arrows have flown beyond him, David must leave because the Lord Himself is sending him away for safety. God often uses hard circumstances to steer His people to safety.

Jonathan reminds David of their covenant, which is a solemn, lifelong promise of loyalty made before God. He declares that the Lord will stand as an eternal witness and judge between them and their families. Their sacred bond remains unbroken even when they are separated by force.
David goes to hide in the open country as they planned. When the monthly festival of the New Moon begins, King Saul sits down to the royal feast.
Saul sits in his usual seat of honor by the wall. Jonathan sits across from him, and Abner the army commander sits by the king's side, but David's place is noticeably empty.
Saul says nothing about David's absence on the first day of the feast. He assumes David has become ceremonially unclean, which means temporarily unfit under God's law to eat a sacred meal.

David's seat remains empty on the second day of the celebration. Saul asks Jonathan why the son of Jesse has missed the meal two days in a row, using David's family name to show contempt rather than calling him his son-in-law.
Jonathan answers his father using the excuse he and David agreed on beforehand. He explains that David earnestly begged for permission to go home to Bethlehem.

Jonathan explains that David's family was holding an annual sacrifice and feast in Bethlehem, and David's older brother ordered him to attend. This gave a proper family reason for why David missed the king's table.

Saul flies into a rage at Jonathan for taking David's side. He hurls a harsh insult calling Jonathan a rebellious son who brings shame on himself and his mother by choosing David over his own royal family.

Saul warns Jonathan that the prince will never secure his own throne as long as David is alive on earth. Driven by jealousy, Saul demands that David be hunted down and brought to him so he can be put to death.
Jonathan bravely speaks up to defend his innocent friend. He asks his father what crime David has committed that would justify putting him to death.
Saul hurls his spear at his own son to strike him down. This violent outburst convinces Jonathan beyond doubt that his father is fully determined to murder David.
Jonathan gets up from the feast in fierce anger and refuses to eat any food that day. He is deeply hurt and grieved by the shameful, violent way his father treated David.
The next morning, Jonathan goes out to the field at the planned time to deliver the news to David. He brings a young boy along to retrieve arrows so his visit looks like ordinary target practice.
Jonathan tells the boy to run and find the arrows he shoots. While the boy is running, Jonathan deliberately shoots an arrow far past him.
When the boy gets near the spot, Jonathan shouts that the arrow is farther ahead. This loud command gives the secret warning to David, who is hiding nearby and listening closely.
Jonathan shouts for the boy to make haste and not delay. Although spoken to the boy to speed him up, these words also tell David that his life is in immediate danger and he must flee at once.
The young helper does not know the true meaning of the shooting and shouting. Only Jonathan and David understand the secret signal they had arranged between them.
Jonathan hands his bow, arrows, and quiver to the boy and tells him to carry them back to town. Sending the servant away gives the two friends a chance to meet face to face without being seen.

Once the boy leaves, David comes out from behind his hiding rock and bows to the ground three times to show honor to Jonathan as the prince. The two friends embrace, kiss, and weep together, with David weeping even more because he is losing his home, his family, and public worship.

Jonathan tells David to go in peace, resting on the solemn oath they made before the Lord to protect each other and their descendants forever. David leaves as a wandering exile, and Jonathan walks back into the city.
